message.content:
Triangulation metrics are quantitative measures that describe the geometric quality and characteristics of a triangulated mesh or network. In the context of your API, they likely refer to statistics computed from the triangulation runs that were performed on products and branches over the last 90 days. Typical triangulation metrics include:

| Metric | What it tells you | Typical use |
|--------|-------------------|-------------|
| **Average triangle area** | Gives an idea of the overall granularity of the mesh. | Helps compare resolution across runs. |
| **Minimum/maximum triangle area** | Highlights extreme cases (very small or very large triangles). | Useful for detecting outliers or poorly conditioned meshes. |
| **Aspect ratio** | Ratio of the longest side to the shortest altitude. | Indicates how “stretched” triangles are; high aspect ratios can degrade numerical stability. |
| **Minimum/maximum internal angle** | Measures how close triangles are to being degenerate (angles near 0° or 180°). | Helps assess mesh quality; very small angles can cause problems in finite‑element analyses. |
| **Edge length distribution** | Histogram or statistical summary of edge lengths. | Useful for understanding mesh density variations. |
| **Number of triangles** | Total count of elements in the mesh. | Basic size metric. |
| **Mesh connectivity statistics** | Average node degree, presence of isolated nodes, etc. | Gives insight into the topological structure. |

When you call the `requests_get` function with the appropriate parameters, the API will return a JSON payload containing these metrics for each triangulation run that occurred within the specified time window. These metrics allow you to evaluate the quality of the triangulations, compare different runs, and identify potential issues that may affect downstream processing or analysis.
